title: China-to-Switzerland EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Connector Redesign — IEC 62196 Type 2 and CCS2
rows.target_requirement: Switzerland-facing EV charging projects are commonly aligned with European IEC connector practice: Type 2 for AC charging and CCS Combo 2 for DC where the project, operator, fleet, or vehicle requirement specifies that interface. Connector selection is a technical interoperability requirement and should not be treated as proof of full market conformance alone.
target_standards: IEC 62196-3:2022 CCS Combo 2 configuration FF ecosystem
Project, fleet, operator, public procurement, and grid-facing interface requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China product evidence commonly references GB/T 20234.2 for AC connectors, GB/T 20234.3 for DC connectors, and GB/T 27930 for charger-to-BMS communication. These should be remapped with full connector, cable, locking, communication, and safety revalidation before claiming Switzerland-facing Type 2 or CCS2 readiness.
rows.gap: If the source kit is GB/T-only, prepare a CH-facing hardware and protocol transition plan: connector housings, pilot/proximity control, pilot logic changes, cable ratings, interlock and lock behaviour, CCS2 control and PLC changes, and controlled validation package for each firmware/variant.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where the Swiss project, procurement contract, charging fleet, or vehicle mix specifies Type 2 and/or CCS2.
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T connector evidence is a China domestic baseline only and does not replace Type 2 or CCS2 readiness proof.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not claim Type 2 or CCS2 readiness from a GB/T-only evidence package. Connector hardware, protocol, and safety features must be revalidated for the exact Switzerland-facing model.

rows.requirement: Swissgrid and Distribution-Network Coordination for EV Charging Sites
rows.target_requirement: EV chargers connected to Swiss distribution networks should follow Swissgrid and local operator review for connection point, power level, load impact, protection settings, meter class, and grid interconnection documentation. This is project-specific and generally includes load study outputs and commissioning evidence for the target Swiss site, regardless of origin.
target_standards: ElCom and utility service framework for load control and metering data
rows.china_equivalent: China domestic interconnection evidence in GB/T 18487 and utility acceptance pathways supports technical preparation, but does not replace Swissgrid or local operator project interconnection requirements for Swiss destination sites.
rows.gap: The practical gap is often not equipment design alone, but operator documentation and settings lock. Exporters should prepare site-specific load studies, utility request letters, commissioning tests, protection coordination tables, and metering outputs for the Switzerland deployment.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for grid-connected EV charging that needs Swiss distribution network interconnection and commissioning approvals.
mandatory_status.cn: China domestic interconnection records support technical comparison only, not Swiss destination approvals.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Keep EV charger safety evidence separate from network-operator connection evidence and local commissioning outputs, even when origin product files are complete.

rows.requirement: Switzerland Market-Side Conformity and Service Framework
rows.target_requirement: Swiss chargers should be assessed under a project-specific market-side path where import clearance, customs classification, charging-service obligations, and operational data obligations are handled by the importer, operator, and network context. Switzerland is not in the EEA, so CE acceptance relies on bilateral MRA and Swiss-adopted routes rather than automatic EEA inference.
target_standards: Switzerland import customs rules for electrical equipment
ElCom framework on network tariffs and consumer-facing charging operations
Local project procurement and contractual requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China product documentation can include CCC where applicable, GB/T 18487.1, GB/T 20234/27930, and domestic market readiness packages. These are useful for technical preparation but do not replace Switzerland-specific market-path obligations or ElCom-related operations checks.
china_standards: China export and market documentation for EV chargers
rows.gap: Exporters should prepare Switzerland-facing market documentation by model, owner, importer, public or private charging scope, pricing and payment architecture, data and reporting requirements, and service operation responsibilities before claiming market readiness.

mandatory_status.target: Project- and service-specific. Mandatory where market operation, network integration, and local contract requirements apply.
mandatory_status.cn: China domestic market or CCC status does not itself satisfy Switzerland-facing market-side obligations.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Product technical files do not replace Switzerland market-side obligations. Verify ElCom-related operations requirements and import-route documentation for each deployment model.

rows.requirement: OCPP Backend Interoperability and Security Profile
rows.target_requirement: OCPP is the global open communication protocol between EV charging stations and charging-management systems. Open Charge Alliance currently lists OCPP 1.6, OCPP 2.0.1, and OCPP 2.1 options. Switzerland-facing projects may require OCPP based on operator backend, automation integration, roaming, payment, or maintenance specifications even when OCPP is not the whole-unit product approval route.
rows.china_equivalent: China-market charging systems often use GB/T 27930 for charger-to-vehicle battery-management communication. That protocol is not a substitute for OCPP backend interoperability, cybersecurity profile, remote firmware workflow, and operator endpoint evidence required in Swiss deployments.
rows.gap: The Switzerland file should define exact OCPP version, security profile, authentication and certificate handling, meter-value mapping, transaction semantics, remote maintenance process, SIM or Ethernet design, and operator acceptance test evidence before integration.

mandatory_status.target: Usually mandatory when operator, roaming, billing, or maintenance specification requires backend interoperability; not itself whole-unit safety certification.
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 27930 does not prove OCPP interoperability for Switzerland-facing backend integration.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm OCPP version and security profile with the Swiss operator before shipment and commissioning. China-only protocol evidence cannot replace operator-facing backend interoperability.

rows.requirement: EMC, Low-Voltage Safety, and Residual-Current Protection
rows.target_requirement: Switzerland-facing EV chargers usually require conformity evidence for applicable electrical safety and electromagnetic compatibility routes. For EVSE, IEC 61851-1 covers core electrical-safety requirements while EMC and installation evidence should align with Swiss-facing project settings, especially RCD type and arrangement for the selected grid interface.
target_standards: Directive 2014/35/EU Low Voltage Directive, CE route as applied through Switzerland recognition
Directive 2014/30/EU EMC framework as aligned in Swiss adoption pathways
IEC 61851-21.2 or Swiss-facing EMC test route where applicable
rows.china_equivalent: China evidence may include GB/T 18487.1, GB/T 18487.2, and related safety or test files. These are useful for technical comparison but must be mapped to Swiss-facing IEC/EN EVSE requirements and local installation assumptions.
rows.gap: The gap is often installation assumptions and parameter integrity: earthing, upstream breaker coordination, RCD or RDC-DD type, DC leakage handling, EMC layout, surge protection, fault current limits, and multilingual warnings for the Swiss site.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where applicable Swiss-facing electrical and EMC laws or project/operator requirements apply, and where installation risk requires fixed protection design evidence.
mandatory_status.cn: China GB/T safety and EMC evidence supports comparison but does not automatically satisfy Switzerland-facing safety and market use requirements.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Validate Switzerland-facing electrical and EMC evidence against the actual installation route, grid point, voltage class, and operator requirements before claiming readiness.
